00675.title: Alternating ifosfamide/etoposide and vincristine/doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide · every 2 weeks: treatment and checks
00675.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00675.setting: Adolescents and young adults with newly diagnosed Ewing-family sarcoma, or the separately listed rhabdomyosarcoma/desmoplastic intra-abdominal small round blue cell tumour indication
00675.summary: There are 14 alternating administrations, planned every 14 days after recovery, not 14 pairs. Ifosfamide and etoposide are given on days 1–5 in cycles 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Vincristine, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide are given on day 1 in cycles 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Cycles 12 and 14 contain vincristine and cyclophosphamide with no doxorubicin; dactinomycin may be added only if the consultant selects it. Surgery, radiotherapy, toxicity or delayed recovery may change the sequence or dates.

milestones.title: Treatment review
milestones.why: Treat cancer throughout the body as part of a specialist plan that also addresses local tumour control. The intended benefit depends on the exact tumour, disease extent and treatment aim.
milestones.clinical: There are 14 alternating administrations, planned every 14 days after recovery, not 14 pairs. Ifosfamide and etoposide are given on days 1–5 in cycles 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Cycles 12 and 14 contain vincristine and cyclophosphamide with no doxorubicin; dactinomycin may be added only if the consultant selects it. Surgery, radiotherapy, toxicity or delayed recovery may change the sequence or dates.
milestones.action: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. 00504.title: Irinotecan and temozolomide: treatment and checks
00504.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00504.summary: Irinotecan 50 mg/m² intravenously and temozolomide 100 mg/m² by mouth are given on days 1–5 of each 21-day cycle. The national plan specifies 6 cycles unless progression, toxicity or the specialist plan changes treatment. Take temozolomide fasting, swallowed whole with water, at least one hour before irinotecan. If you vomit after temozolomide, do not take an extra dose.

milestones.title: Treatment review
milestones.why: Aim to shrink or control cancer and help symptoms after previous treatment. Your specialist explains the realistic benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for your particular disease.
milestones.clinical: Irinotecan 50 mg/m² intravenously and temozolomide 100 mg/m² by mouth are given on days 1–5 of each 21-day cycle. The national plan specifies 6 cycles unless progression, toxicity or the specialist plan changes treatment. Take temozolomide fasting, swallowed whole with water, at least one hour before irinotecan. If you vomit after temozolomide, do not take an extra dose.
milestones.action: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. Irinotecan can cause two different bowel problems. Cramping, sweating and diarrhoea during or shortly after infusion can be an acute cholinergic reaction: tell the nurse immediately; prescribed atropine may be used. Delayed diarrhoea begins more than 24 hours later and can cause dangerous dehydration or infection. Contact oncology at the first loose stool and follow the written anti-diarrhoeal and rehydration prescription. Fever, severe pain, blood, faintness, very little urine or inability to drink needs immediate assessment; never wait for a time threshold when seriously unwell. Report a new cough, breathlessness, jaundice, severe rash or marked weakness urgently.

00757.title: Vincristine, irinotecan and temozolomide: treatment and checks
00757.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00757.summary: Irinotecan 50 mg/m² is given intravenously on days 1–5 of each 21-day cycle. Temozolomide is taken by mouth on days 1–5: 125 mg/m² in cycle 1. Only the treating team may select 150 mg/m² from cycle 2 after toxicity review. Vincristine 1.5 mg/m², maximum 2 mg, is given on days 1 and 8. The national plan specifies 12 cycles unless progression, toxicity or the specialist plan changes treatment. Take temozolomide fasting, swallowed whole with water, at least one hour before irinotecan. If you vomit after temozolomide, do not take an extra dose.

00754.title: Ifosfamide, vincristine, dactinomycin and doxorubicin: treatment and checks
00754.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00754.setting: High-risk or very-high-risk rhabdomyosarcoma in people younger than 40 years
00754.summary: Nine cycles are planned every 21 days. In cycles 1–2, vincristine is given on days 1, 8 and 15; doxorubicin on days 1 and 2; dactinomycin on day 1; and ifosfamide on days 1 and 2. In cycles 3–4, vincristine is given only on day 1, with the other three drugs on the same days as before. In cycles 5–9, doxorubicin is omitted; day-1 vincristine/dactinomycin and day-1/2 ifosfamide continue. Use the correct phase chart for your actual cycle.
